$comment: Your Tier 3 instance. This file is the authority for what YOUR machine installs. It pins Tier 2 (the shared __ORG_DISPLAY__ environment) and lists ONLY your personal additions — it deliberately does not re-list Tier 2's skills, because a second copy of that list is a drift waiting to happen. install.sh fetches Tier 2, delegates to its installer for the shared skills and hooks, then layers whatever you declare below on top.
$agentNameNote: Empty until the agent chooses. This is deliberately NOT defaulted from the instance name — a name that arrived by default was never chosen. Start a session, ask your agent to pick one, then set it here and export AGENT_NAME. It must NEVER be used as a release, image tag, or ticket fixVersion — those use the application name plus semver.

__ORG_LAYER_NAME__.role: Tier 2 — the shared __ORG_DISPLAY__ environment. Brings Tier 1 with it.
__ORG_LAYER_NAME__.$refNote: A COMMIT SHA, resolved when this instance was generated. Deliberate: a branch name here means upstream can move under you between installs, and a release branch moves most while it is under review — exactly when new people are onboarding. Pinned, an upstream change can never surprise you mid-task. Taking an update stays a one-line bump, but it happens when you choose. $refSource records the branch this SHA came from, so you know where to look for the next one.

install.$comment: YOUR additions only. Anything here is layered AFTER Tier 2, so a same-named entry overrides Tier 2's — which is how you customise a shared skill without forking the shared repo. Overriding is reported loudly by install.sh, because a silent override is how tiers rot. A name in the `skills`/`hooks` ARRAY is the declaration; the matching `skillSources`/`hookSources` entry says where it comes from. Both halves are required: either alone installs nothing while still reading like a declaration, and install.sh reports both directions.

skillSources.$comment: skill-name -> source. Prefix `local:` for a skill this instance owns outright, e.g. "my-skill": "local:skills/my-skill" — `local:` resolves against THIS lockfile's directory, so it still means your instance when the installer is a vendored copy. `upstream:<path>` (or a bare path) resolves under vendorDir. A value containing '..' is refused. Keys beginning with $ are documentation, not entries.

hookSources.$comment: hook-file-name -> source. Same rules as skillSources.

notRestorable.gh auth login: credentials cannot live in a lockfile
notRestorable.MCP connectors: authenticated interactively — confirm your tool namespace before relying on it
notRestorable.settings.json hook registration: yours to edit — the installer places files, it will not touch your settings
